title: The code itself: unused, copied, packages, files
grade_reasons: The base is the tidiest in the review: about 2,700 of 772,000 lines are dead (0.35%), 0.87% are exact copies across files, no package is unused and all 150 public files are referenced. But not one of those numbers is held by a test (lint sees unused locals only), so by the scale it cannot be an A, and without budgets it is not a B either: the draft's A rested on the counts alone. And the waste is real: 14 twin file pairs share more than 50 lines (five imports, two accounting syncs, the platform's second engines, Work drawn twice), kaizenaflow.com is kept twice (up to 4,400 lines), every admin page loads 354 KB of libraries it does not call, a 3x phone downloads the 1,600 px file for each product tile, and search thumbnails of uploaded pictures answer 400. The findings this area owns about what server functions load (the schema, sharp, both languages of the admin's words) are graded in the server area.

measures.name: Dead code: exports nothing uses, and production code only a test keeps alive
measures.today: 331 exports (721 lines) used by nothing; 3 dead files (171 lines); 443 exports (2,959 lines) named only by tests, about 330 of them dead but for the test. About 2,700 dead lines in all, 0.35% of 772,235. Source: digest/unused-code.md and m/dead.md.
measures.target_a: 0 exports used by nothing. 0 files only tests reach outside named test support and a list with reasons. Every export only tests import is in keptForTests with its reason: at most 130 names (the oracles, about 500 lines). Dead lines under 0.05% (under 400).
measures.how_measured: docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/unused-code.mjs today. After the work item for DD-4: src/server/unused.scan.test.ts with scripts/unused.mjs and src/server/unused.baseline.json.
measures.why_this_is_a: The floor is not zero lines. Invoice and credit-note oracles and reset helpers exist for tests by design, and the scan cannot see inside a file that is namespace-imported (about 13 exports, 30 lines). So the tolerance is a list of at most 130 names, each with a reason, and nothing unlisted. A B would be a count that may only fall; an A is exact lists, so one dead export cannot take another's place.

measures.name: Copied lines
measures.today: Exact copies: 4,803 of 472,586 code lines (1.02%); 4,098 across files (0.87%), 705 inside one file. Near-copies with names and literals normalised: 22,429 (4.75%). Source: digest/copied-code.md (the review's detector, work/cp/near.mjs).
measures.target_a: Exact copies across files at most 0.6% (2,850 lines), failing the test above that. Near-copies at most 3.7%, printed with the ten largest pairs on each run.
measures.how_measured: The review's detector as scripts/lib/copy-count.mjs, run by the copy test against src/lib/copies.baseline.json (work item for CP-14 and FM-13). The detector is not in the repo yet: gap 1.
measures.why_this_is_a: Data that is parallel by design (catalogues, the schema, signature themes, API catalogue entries) is set aside, not counted. About 7,100 near-copied lines across files could be extracted at all; if every one went the share would be 3.2%, and about 1,400 lines are per-language text that only looks alike. An A is within half a point of that floor. Today's 0.87% exact is already under the 3% most tools call good, which is why the bar is set from the floor and not from a tool's default.

measures.why_this_is_a: Some pairs are honest parallels: two carriers' booking shims, a test helper that mirrors a reader. Eight pairs of at most 50 lines is under 400 shared lines, less than 0.1% of the code. A B would hold today's 41. An A has no engine written twice: one import definition, one workflow and delivery engine with a scope, one Work view, one accounting sync core, one site.

measures.name: Hand-made repeats too small for a copy detector: helpers and admin controls
measures.today: fail() is declared in 43 server files, isUuid in 23, isUniqueViolation in 9; addDays, daysBetween, isDay and countryName have 31 declarations with up to 6 bodies. 284 input, field, card, label and hint class constants in 171 admin files; 154 hand-written tables; 436 native selects. 232 of 235 admin action files are off the shared wrapper, 23 with a guard wrapper of their own. A store's address by id is looked up by hand in 27 places. Source: digest/copied-code.md and digest/families.md; the 27 re-counted with rg.
measures.target_a: Each helper declared once (isUuid and isUniqueViolation 2 declarations in all; the day and country helpers at most 8 with re-exports; the store-address lookup at most 3). Class constants under 100. No local guard wrapper (23 today). Tables, selects and off-wrapper files are counts in the ratchet that only fall.
measures.how_measured: The rg counts of the planners' done-whens; seven new counts in scripts/lib/ratchet-count.mjs and src/server/ratchet.baseline.json (FM-7, FM-8); a lint rule for the helper names (FM-12).
measures.why_this_is_a: These repeats are below any copy window, so no detector sees them: they need their own counts. The floor is one declaration per helper. A kit cannot cover every one-off layout, so 100 class constants (a third of today's) is the tolerance. The 209 action files left off the wrapper cost no lines, so an A asks only that their number is held and falls.

measures.name: Files stored and served
measures.today: public/: 150 files, 5.6 MB, 0 unreferenced, checked once by hand; six flags weigh 165 KB. Lifetimes: public files max-age=0; font files are not kept by the CDN; videos, 3D models and field files get 1 hour and theme photographs 5 minutes though their addresses never change (0 of 9 browser upload calls set a lifetime); pictures get 1 year. Each picture is kept in 2 sizes (480 and 1,600 px), so a 3x phone takes the 1,600 px file for a tile (71 KB where 18 KB would do). /_next/image is open and answers 400 for uploaded pictures, so search thumbnails are empty. Source: digest/assets.md; the upload calls and the font header re-checked with rg.
measures.target_a: 0 unreferenced public files, held by a test; flags under 20 KB. Every file with a fixed address is kept a year (public files a day): 9 of 9 upload calls set it, and the second request for a font file is a CDN hit. A tile at 390 px and 3x takes the 800 px file. /_next/image answers 404 and the search box draws stored thumbnails.
measures.how_measured: A public-files case in the unused scan (gap 2); curl -sI on a public file, a font file and an uploaded video; rg -n 'uploadToSignedUrl' src/components; the new test of currentSrc in e2e/performance.spec.ts; e2e/search.spec.ts.
measures.why_this_is_a: A file must be fetched once per browser: that is the floor. Public files keep one conditional request a day because their names can be reused. Three stored widths, not five, is the tolerance: a 2x phone may still take a file up to a third wider than it needs.

measures.name: Checks that hold these numbers
measures.today: 0 of 7. Lint fails on an unused local, never on an unused export. No test counts copies, twins, admin repeats, packages, public files, or what a route loads and carries; the ratchet holds four other counts. Source: rg over package.json, eslint.config.mjs, .github and the scan tests.
measures.target_a: 7 of 7 run in pnpm test or CI: the unused scan, the copy and twin baseline, the admin repeat counts, the dependency scan, the public-files and route-handler case, the route-load graph test and the trace report. Each is proven once by a trial edit that makes it fail.
